subject: Vector snapshot & backup — commercial / ops handoff
messages:
From: Amaya Singh <amaya@pinecone.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@pinecone.io
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + snapshot/backup pilot (Pinecone <> Redwood)

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Pinecone is seeing more customers ask for durable snapshotting of their vector indexes for disaster recovery, analytics, and cross-region migration. We have a small set of customers who would like a snapshot to S3 workflow and an ops+commercial model for ongoing backups.

We proposed a light pilot: Pinecone will export periodic snapshots to an S3 bucket; Redwood will validate restore flows and confirm compatibility with your index formats and our KV cache/replay. High level asks from our side:
- Verify we can restore a snapshot into a Redwood-backed runtime within the expected RTO (target: <30m for a 100M-index test)
- Confirm metadata/versions are preserved and deduped across incremental snapshots
- Validate cost and retention policy recommendations (hot vs cold)

We typically run pilots with a 2–3 week technical validation and then a handoff SOW for production retention. Are you able to run a kickoff the week of 6/14? Marcus from NimbusAI (cc'd) has offered to help with the S3 lifecycle and retention modeling.

Attaching a short diagram of the snapshot flow for context (vector-snapshot-arch.png).

Best,
Amaya
Partner Lead, Pinecone

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Amaya Singh <amaya@pinecone.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@nimbusai.co>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + snapshot/backup pilot (Pinecone <> Redwood)

Amaya —

Thanks, this looks like a good and pragmatic pilot. We can run a kickoff on Tue 6/15 at 10am PT. Proposed scope we want to cover during the pilot kickoff:
1) Concrete test dataset + target index size (we suggest a 50–150M vector index for realistic timing)
2) Snapshot frequency and incremental snapshot semantics
3) S3 bucket setup: permissions, KMS key, lifecycle rules (glacier/cold tier)
4) Restore exercise: target RTO / RPO and verification checks
5) Operational responsibilities and alerting (who restores, who pays for storage)
6) Success criteria to move to SOW (performance, data integrity, costs)

I've looped in Marissa to lead the commercial SOW and Jonas/Laura to lead the ops/runbook work. Marcus — appreciate NimbusAI helping with lifecycle costing.

Ben
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intro + snapshot/backup pilot — commercial questions

Folks — forwarding Amaya's note. Quick commercial checklist I want covered before the kickoff:
- Do we want a retainer vs a per-GB storage pass-through? (I prefer a small retainer + pass-through for heavy egress restores)
- Contract length for production backups (12 vs 36 months) and early termination terms
- Liability / SLA for restore RTO — Pinecone has customers requiring 24/7 DR support; if they want SLA-backed restores we need to scope on-call runbooks and pricing
- Data residency requirements (we may need EU bucket options for some joint customers)

I will prepare a SOW skeleton and send ahead of the meeting. Jonas — can you mock up a minimal runbook template we can use to estimate ops hours?

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Partnerships

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro + snapshot/backup pilot — runbook draft

Marissa / Ben —

Attached is a one-page runbook outline I'll bring to the kickoff. Highlights:
- Snapshot ingestion steps (credentials, validation checksums, manifest parsing)
- Restore orchestration: slot the restore into a staging cluster, replay KV caches, smoke-test 10 sample queries across latency bands
- Estimated manual ops time for a single full-restore (100M vectors): 3.5 engineer-hours on average during pilot; 1.2 hours after automation improvements
- Permissions: we prefer temporary STS creds scoped to the snapshot prefix rather than long-lived keys

I'll also include quick checklist items for security/compliance to link back to our SOC 2 questionnaire.

Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Amaya Singh <amaya@pinecone.io>, Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@nimbusai.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + snapshot/backup pilot (Pinecone <> Redwood) — kickoff confirmed + pre-reads

Amaya / Marcus —

Confirmed for Tue 6/15 10am PT (calendar invite sent). Action items we will bring to that meeting:
- Redwood: runbook draft (jonas), SOW skeleton (marissa), security checklist + SOC 2 pointer (laura)
- Pinecone: sample index manifest and one export (small sample) for our validation; pointer to preferred S3 bucket naming + KMS policy
- NimbusAI: lifecycle cost model and suggested retention tiers for pilot (hot/warm/cold)

Pre-reads attached: RINF-Pinecone-SOW-draft-v1.pdf, vector-snapshot-arch.png. If Pinecone needs us to sign an NDA for the sample export, please send ahead of time.

High-level commercial note: Marissa and I agree to start with a 3-month pilot with a small monthly retainer (TBD) and pass-through for storage; we will firm up pricing in the SOW draft during week 1 of the pilot.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Ben
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
